requirements.BS-KIT-001: The chart is built from `SafetyViz.kit`, found on the page: safety.viz's bundle and bio.viz's are two script tags, and the shell, the sidebar and the controls are the kit's. On a page without safety.viz the chart refuses to be made, with a message saying that `SafetyViz.kit` was not found.
requirements.BS-KIT-002: bio.viz's committed bundles export `biomarkerScreen`, hold none of safety.viz, no Chart.js and no webR, and defining the chart needs no safety.viz.
requirements.BS-KIT-003: The chart is built from the parts every chart shares, in `src/shared/`, and none of them is written a second time in its own files: the paging of a long list, the way back and the reading of participant-level numbers among them, shared with the charts that had them. Of other charts it imports their public functions alone, `groupComparison` and `associationScatter`, to open a row; nothing under their folders and nothing of the correlation matrix; and no other chart imports anything of this one.
requirements.BS-KIT-004: The chart's source holds no statistical inference: no arithmetic of an estimate, an interval, a p-value or an adjustment, and nothing ordered by a key R did not return. What it works out from R's numbers is where a dot and a line sit along the shared axis and how far that axis runs.
requirements.BS-CFG-001: The chart has the settings the reference lists, with these defaults: the core's column and baseline settings; `comparison` `difference`, with `visit`, `group_by`, `levels` and `with` null, so it opens on every biomarker at the first visit between the first two groups of the first column of groups; `value_type` `raw`; `method` `pearson`; `adjustment` `BH`; `sort` `estimate`; `limit` 20; and `statistic` `Analyze_Screen`.
requirements.BS-CFG-002: A setting that is not known, or a value a setting cannot take, is refused with a `TypeError` whose message begins `bio.viz:` and names the setting; `levels` names exactly two groups, and `with` is a variable as the core takes one.
requirements.BS-DATA-001: The rows are the biomarkers of the Biomarker list, in its order, each at the one visit with the one value type; a baseline value is read with no visit.
requirements.BS-DATA-002: For a correlation, a biomarker that is the fixed variable itself is not a row of its own, and the note says so. With no column of two groups, no fixed variable, or a change at the one baseline visit, there is nothing to screen, and the chart says why and what to choose.
requirements.BS-DATA-003: The frame is the core's: one row per participant, one column per biomarker named by the biomarker, none required, so a participant missing some is kept with a gap; beside them the column of groups or the fixed variable. A participant with none of the biomarkers is left out and counted; the filters choose participants first; two columns of one name are refused in words.
requirements.BS-DATA-004: A difference's two groups are the two chosen when the column has both, and otherwise the column's first two, in order; the estimate is the first's less the second's.
requirements.BS-DATA-005: The rows are ordered by R's estimate, largest first, by name, or by R's adjusted p-value, smallest first; a row R gave no number for comes after those it did, rows that tie keep R's order, and no key is made that R did not return.
requirements.BS-DATA-006: Every row is drawn on one axis without units: for a difference it runs symmetrically about nought far enough to hold every interval R returned, with round labels; for a correlation from −1 to 1; nought is always on it.
requirements.BS-LIMIT-001: With more rows than `limit`, the rows are paged: a page holds at most `limit` of them in the order sorted, a page that does not exist is brought back to the nearest that does, and the note says how many are shown of how many, in what order and how many to a page.
requirements.BS-LIMIT-002: On the page, Previous and Next go between the pages of rows, which page of how many is said, the rows are the sorted rows of that page, and R is not asked again.
requirements.BS-CTRL-001: The sidebar offers what the design asks: the comparison, the value type and the visit; for a difference the column of groups and its first and second group; for a correlation the fixed variable, a participant-level number or a biomarker with its visit, and the method; the adjustment; the order; a filter per category column of the participant table; and Reset chart. A baseline value has no Visit control.
requirements.BS-CTRL-002: A change to the comparison, the value, the visit, the column of groups, a group, the fixed variable, the method, the adjustment or a filter draws the screen again for what was chosen and asks R again with it; the same group chosen twice swaps the two; Reset chart returns every control to what the chart opened on.
requirements.BS-CTRL-003: A change to the order draws the rows R returned in another order and asks R nothing.
requirements.BS-CTRL-004: With the setting `statistic` null the chart has no Statistics controls, asks R for nothing and draws no rows.
requirements.BS-DRAW-001: The demo's view, every biomarker's change from Baseline to Week 4 between the arms, draws one row per biomarker sorted by R's estimate, largest first, with IL-6 at the top: its estimate a dot and its interval a line where R's numbers put them on the one axis, nought marked, and beside them the estimate with its interval, the unadjusted and the adjusted p-value and each group's count.
requirements.BS-DRAW-002: Every row is a button whose name is the whole row in a sentence from the shared formatter: the estimate, its interval, the method, the unadjusted and the adjusted p-value and the counts. A caption says what the estimate is, at what level its interval is, which test the p-values are and by what they were adjusted across how many biomarkers, and the line under the screen says the same of R's answer, once.
requirements.BS-DRAW-003: Every p-value is printed with its method and counts and labelled exploratory, the adjusted one with the adjustment by name; no star and no word such as significant is printed anywhere, for either adjustment or comparison.
requirements.BS-DRAW-004: A row R could not compute shows R's reason, as R worded it, and no number, no dot and no line, and says it is not in the adjustment; where no row could be computed the line gives R's reason.
requirements.BS-DRAW-005: A correlation screen against IL-10 at Baseline draws every other biomarker on an axis from −1 to 1, with TNF-alpha at the top; for Spearman no interval is drawn or printed, none being made up.
requirements.BS-DRAW-006: Above the screen the chart says how many participants are in the frame of how many and how many were left out for having none of the biomarkers; under it, that each row is of the participants who have its biomarker, so each row has its own counts, as R counted them.
requirements.BS-LIST-001: The rows download as a CSV file under this chart's name, in the order shown, with the estimate, the interval, both p-values, the counts and R's reason where there is no number.
requirements.BS-STAT-001: The screen asks R once, whatever the number of rows: the function named in `statistic`, the frame, the biomarkers as `chrCols`, the comparison, the column of groups and the two groups for a difference or the fixed variable's column and the method for a correlation, and the adjustment. The identity of the frame names the chart, the value type, the visit, the baseline settings, the fixed variable and the filters in force.
requirements.BS-STAT-002: R's answer is described without computing anything: the method as R names it, how many rows R computed of how many, and the adjustment by name across the number of rows R adjusted across; R's notes and warnings as R worded them; R's reason where no row could be computed; R's error as an error; and a result that names no method, or whose rows were not adjusted as one family, is refused.
requirements.BS-STAT-003: Each row is formatted by the shared formatter, and R's numbers are kept beside it for the dot, the line and the order only for a row R computed; a row is in the adjustment when R says it adjusted across it.
requirements.BS-STAT-004: From the moment the screen is asked for until R answers, the line reads that it is waiting, with the page's note until R has answered once, and no rows are drawn: the chart says which biomarkers it will screen. Then the rows and the line are drawn from R's answer.
requirements.BS-STAT-005: A change that asks R again clears the rows and the line; an answer to the question before is dropped when it arrives, and is never shown.
requirements.BS-STAT-006: With no R attached the line says that statistics are unavailable and no rows are drawn: the chart says which biomarkers it would screen; nothing is fetched to say so.
requirements.BS-STAT-007: With R's answers stored in the page the rows are drawn from them with no R and no request; a view no result was stored for says so and draws no rows, never another view's.
requirements.BS-STAT-008: `chart.statistics()` returns what the chart asked R for the screen now drawn and what R answered: one entry, with the function, the arguments, the identity and the number of rows.
requirements.BS-STAT-009: For every case of the expected results, the function, the arguments, the identity and the row count that R wrote by the recipe in the reference are the ones the chart asks with; handed to a connection as stored results each is found by the chart's request, and by no other view's; and the recipe in the reference is the script's.
requirements.BS-STAT-010: The frames desktop R is run on are written by the chart's own code from the demo's own tables and settings, and committed; deriving them again gives the committed files. A gap is an empty cell.
requirements.BS-STAT-011: The expected results name the script, the R version and the vendored statistics file that made them, and hold one result per case: both comparisons and both adjustments, a filter, another column of groups, a participant-level number, and a view whose every row has a group too small, those rows left out of the adjustment as R says.
requirements.BS-STAT-012: In desktop R's answers the planted biomarkers are the top rows by estimate: IL-6's change from Baseline to Week 4 between the arms, and TNF-alpha against IL-10 at Baseline, whose interval holds 0.6. A difference row's unadjusted p-value is the group comparison's Welch p-value for that biomarker, and a correlation row's coefficient is the association scatter's, each from that chart's own expected results.
requirements.BS-DRILL-001: A click on a row of a difference opens the group comparison for that biomarker in place of the screen, at the same visit and value, with the same column of groups and two groups and Welch's test, and a button back that takes the keyboard's place.
requirements.BS-DRILL-002: A click on a row of a correlation opens the association scatter for that biomarker against the fixed variable, with the same method, and a button back.
requirements.BS-DRILL-003: From the keyboard a row is reached with Tab and opened with Enter or Space; Enter or Space on the button back returns to the screen.
requirements.BS-DRILL-004: The chart a row opens is handed the screen's connection itself, its filters as they are set and the column settings, with the settings `group_comparison` or `association_scatter` beneath. With results stored in the page, the group comparison's Welch p-value is the difference row's unadjusted p-value, and the scatter's coefficient is the correlation row's estimate.
requirements.BS-DRILL-005: Returning shows the screen exactly as it was, on the same page in the same order, with the keyboard on the row that was opened, and R is not asked again for the screen.
requirements.BS-DRILL-006: `chart.open(biomarker)` opens a row's chart by the biomarker's name and returns it, `chart.opened()` gives it while it is open, and `chart.close()` returns to the screen; a name the screen does not have is refused with the names it has. Drawing the screen again closes a chart that is open.
requirements.BS-FILTER-001: On the demo, filters with nobody in common leave the chart reading `No participant passes the filters.`, in the words every chart uses, with the note that none of the participants pass; no rows are drawn, R is asked nothing, the filters and Reset chart stay usable, nothing is written to the console, and loosening a filter draws again.
requirements.BS-FILTER-002: A filter reads its spec by the rule safety.viz's charts follow, through the kit's `reconcileFilters`: `start` sets what it opens on and All is still offered; only `all: false` removes All, and its first value is then the one in force; a value the data lacks falls back to All with a console warning naming the filter; and the selection each control shows is the selection the chart filters by.
requirements.BS-LIFE-001: `init`, `setData`, `setSettings`, `render`, `resize` and `destroy` drive the chart as they drive a safety.viz chart; `setSettings` moves the control of a setting that says what the chart opens on, and `destroy` takes down the screen, a chart a row had opened and everything in the element.
requirements.BS-LIFE-002: Tables the chart cannot read are refused with a `TypeError`, and the message is shown in the chart's place.
requirements.BS-MOBILE-001: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport the chart fills the width with its controls folded away one tap from open; each row stacks its name, its interval on the full width of the axis and its numbers, each named before it, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.BS-MOBILE-002: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport a tap on a row opens its chart and its button returns, and the page does not scroll sideways at any point.
requirements.BS-SITE-001: The gallery lists the biomarker screen with links to its live demo, its evidence page and its API reference.
requirements.BS-SITE-002: The live demo draws the chart on the synthetic study, opening on the planted difference, every biomarker's change from Baseline to Week 4 between the arms, from safety.viz's vendored bundle and bio.viz's committed one, with R attached and gsm.bio's statistics file published beside it. Where R's host cannot be reached it draws no rows, and says that R could not be started.
requirements.BS-SITE-003: The live demo holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll, with the controls open and a row opened in its chart.
requirements.BS-SITE-004: The API reference has a table row for every setting the chart has, with the default the code has; the site build fails when one is missing.
requirements.BS-SITE-005: The demos point at one another: the screen's page says a row opens the group comparison or the association scatter, and the group comparison's and the scatter's pages point to the screen as the way in.
requirements.BS-LIVE-001: The gallery's demo starts R in the browser when the screen first asks, from webR's pinned version and gsm.bio's vendored statistics file, with no R package installed. The line waits, saying what the first start costs, and then every row's estimate, interval, unadjusted and adjusted p-value and counts equal desktop R's within 1 part in 10^8, the rows in the order of R's estimates with IL-6 at the top.
requirements.BS-LIVE-002: On the demo, with Holm's adjustment, every row equals desktop R's.
requirements.BS-LIVE-003: On the demo, the correlation screen against IL-10 at Baseline, by Benjamini-Hochberg and by Holm, and with Spearman's coefficient, equals desktop R's in every row, with TNF-alpha at the top and 0.6 inside its interval; where R's own wording differs between the versions, both are recorded and nothing else differs.
requirements.BS-LIVE-004: On the demo, a change shows the waiting state and then the new screen, which equals desktop R's, and never the old one: with a filter, another column of groups, the result at Baseline, a participant-level number, and a view whose every row has a group too small.
requirements.BS-LIVE-005: On the demo, a row of the difference opens the group comparison, whose Welch p-value from the same R, started once, is the row's unadjusted p-value; a row of the correlation opens the scatter, whose coefficient is the row's; returning shows the screen as it was and asks R nothing.
requirements.BS-LIVE-006: The megabytes and seconds of the demo's first screen, and the seconds R takes for a screen once started, are measured, printed in the run's log and written to a file with both versions' answers, and the megabytes are what the page tells its reader in the waiting text.
requirements.BS-LIVE-007: On a phone the demo draws its rows from R, stacked, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.BS-STAT-013: When the connection is replaced (`setSettings({ connection })`), an answer that arrives late from the connection it replaced is never shown: it changes neither the statistics line nor what `chart.statistics()` reports.
requirements.BS-FAIL-001: When drawing fails, the biomarker screen says so in its footnote (`This chart could not be drawn:` and why), takes away what was drawn of the rows, ends the statistics round, empties the listing and the participant rail, says it in the danger colour and keeps its controls; once drawing works again it draws.
requirements.BS-DROP-001: With a participant table, a participant the results have and the table does not is left out and counted (`Not in the participant table`), and a row of results with no participant id is counted (`Row has no participant id`); a participant table without the participant id column is refused with a sentence that names the column.
requirements.BS-NAME-001: A biomarker whose name has a space at either end is screened under its name as written, and R is handed it by that name.
requirements.BS-DROP-002: With results for participants the participant table does not have and filters that let nobody through, the chart says `No participant passes the filters.`, as it does with no such rows.
requirements.BS-DROP-003: A setting that names a participant id column the participant table does not have (`setSettings({ participant_id_col })`) is refused with the same sentence as the tables are, before anything changes, and the chart stays as it was drawn, a chart opened in place included (bio.viz#52).
requirements.BS-STAT-014: The R recipe run on a data frame with a visit column that holds numbers writes the identity as text, as the chart asks with, so a stored result written that way is found.
requirements.BS-STAT-015: For a difference, the statistics line under the rows prints R's own note that the interval is the pooled-variance interval for Hedges' g while the p-value is Welch's, which does not pool; the chart adds no words of its own about R's methods.
requirements.BS-DROP-004: The participant table and the setting that names its id column change together: `setData(tables, settings)` checks the tables against the settings it is given with them, lays the settings over, and draws.
